originality.rationale: The inspected Nathanson full text explicitly asks in Open Problem 2(b) for n>=3 equality with the greedy sum and multiplicities, while its Section 7 enumerates only selected n=2 ties. Chu (arXiv:2306.12564) treats two terms. Kovač (arXiv:2406.07218) treats almost-everywhere eventual behavior, and Kovač–Tang (arXiv:2607.28387) treats eventual behavior for rational targets; neither implies an exact three-term fiber size for the constructed rational theta. The classical divisor formula for 2/q is credited; the exact large-c stability, globally best perturbation and growing count are additional structural conclusions. Ten actual semantic mathematical-record queries and web equivalents returned no same-claim hit among reviewed candidates; this does not prove uniqueness in literature.

value.rationale: Nathanson explicitly posed whether n>=3 can have a nongreedy tuple with exactly the greedy sum and asked about multiplicities. This theorem gives unbounded multiplicity even for globally best greedy triples, proves an exact count of ALL such tuples for a natural explicit infinite family, and distinguishes equal-vs-distinct denominator conventions. The complete bestness-and-fiber statement is not a mere padded pair identity: proving both maximality under a concrete target and exclusion of other triples requires structural denominator bounds.
